event_overview.title: About Mississippi Homicide
event_overview.subject: Mississippi Homicide
event_overview.summary: This is the homicide investigation into the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old woman whose body was found hanging from a tree behind a vacant home in west Jackson, Mississippi, on August 3, 2026. Authorities later classified the death as a homicide; investigators testified that they believe the hanging occurred after her death, while the precise cause of death had not been publicly disclosed as of September 26, 2026.

facts.label: Discovery and location
facts.value: Fortune was found on August 3, 2026, in the backyard of a vacant home in west Jackson, including reporting that placed the site in the 500 block of Road of Remembrance.

facts.label: Investigating authority
facts.value: The Jackson Police Department is the lead local agency publicly reporting on the case; Chief RaShall Brackney said the state medical examiner's office determined that Fortune's death was a homicide on September 10, 2026.

facts.label: Nature of the allegation
facts.value: At a September 25 court hearing, a Jackson police detective testified, citing the medical examiner's opinion, that Fortune was already dead when her body was hanged and that the scene was staged. That testimony was part of an ongoing criminal case, not a final judicial finding.

facts.label: Criminal proceedings
facts.value: By September 25, authorities had announced murder charges against multiple men; the first defendant, Jarques Ratliff, had pleaded not guilty and was awaiting continuation of a preliminary hearing set for September 30 to determine whether sufficient evidence existed to send the matter to a grand jury.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline follows key publicly reported developments in the investigation and arrests connected to Fortune's death, but does not purport to cover every filing, hearing, investigative lead, or any final adjudication.
